description: §19.16.3 rule 1 reaches EVERY statement position inside a deferred body — including value-form arms that the front-end carries as text: a `return` in a value-form `match` arm block (viaMatchArm), a `fail` in one (viaMatchArmFail), a `return` in an if-as-expression arm (viaIfExpr) and a `return` in a `!{}` handler arm (viaHandlerArm) are each E-DEFER-CONTROL-FLOW — four occurrences. A `return` inside an arrow function passed to `.map` (lambdaIsABoundary) is its own scope and does NOT fire. Unchecked, the arm `return` would leave the function from inside the `finally`, overriding its real return value (viaMatchArm would return 5, not 1).
rationale: §19.16.3 rule 1: a deferred body SHALL NOT contain `return` / `fail` / `?` / an escaping `break`/`continue`, at any depth — value-form match / if arms and `!{}` handler arms included; a nested function or lambda body is its own control-flow scope.
